intro: Kingley Vale is a national nature reserve in the South Downs, about five miles north-west of Chichester in West Sussex, and one of the finest yew forests in Europe. Some of its yews are thought to be up to 2,000 years old. A reader sent us a photograph from among the oldest of them, where trunks and limbs grow into one dim lattice.

trees.story:
"This is an ancient woodland of Yew trees, not one tree but hundreds forming an interlocking lacework of gnarled limbs and twisted trunks," wrote the reader who sent us this photograph from Kingley Vale, north of Chichester.

Kingley Vale holds one of the most impressive yew forests in Europe, and some of its trees are thought to be as much as 2,000 years old, among the oldest living things in Britain. That they survived at all is the remarkable part: across Europe the old yews were felled for longbow staves from the fourteenth century on, and stands like this one became rare.

The photograph shows what the reader means by lacework. On the left rises one great fluted trunk, red under the grey, and from it and its neighbours limbs bend down to the ground, cross each other and climb again, so that the whole grove is one tangle of wood with sunlight coming through in pieces. The reader puts the trees at 500 to 2,000 years and one trunk at about 4.5 metres round; those figures are theirs.

Walk up the valley from West Stoke, and step in under the limbs.

question_context: Kingley Vale, a national nature reserve in the South Downs north-west of Chichester, holds one of the most impressive yew forests in Europe, and some of its trees are thought to be as much as 2,000 years old. That makes them some of the oldest living things in Britain. Their survival is the surprising part: from the fourteenth century the old yews of Europe were cut for longbow staves, and few large stands were left. A reader who walked in among the oldest trees sent us a photograph and called it "an interlocking lacework of gnarled limbs and twisted trunks", and that is what it shows: huge fluted trunks whose limbs bend down, cross and climb again. The reader puts the trees at 500 to 2,000 years and one trunk at about 4.5 metres round. The reserve is managed by Natural England and is free and open at all times. Park at West Stoke and walk up the valley, or take the footpaths up from Stoughton.

faq.q: How old are the yews of Kingley Vale?

faq.q: Why did Kingley Vale's yews survive?
faq.a: Most of Europe's old yews were felled for longbow staves from the fourteenth century on; Kingley Vale is one of the few large stands that remained.
